faithfulness_notes: Fully implementable; nothing had to be invented. G_n was transcribed verbatim from solution lines 0007-0020 (edge set, delta_i = 2^(i-2), W, all four weight rules). The algorithm is the one the solution analyses at lines 0074-0080: Dijkstra from v1 with a min-heap, negative edges permitted, and a vertex re-inserted whenever its tentative distance improves ('no permanent closed status'). The one point of genuine underspecification is what 'revisited' means operationally, so BOTH readings were implemented and reported: (a) lazy re-insertion with stale-entry skipping, and (b) never-skip, where every popped heap entry re-relaxes its tail's outgoing edges -- the maximally generous reading for the solution. Neither approaches the claimed bound. The second underspecification is tie-breaking among equal keys; the solution asserts 'the analysis is symmetric regardless of which intermediate is chosen at each step' (lines 0100-0103) and traces v2, v3, ..., which the smallest-index tie-break reproduces, and Step D additionally searches all legal orders exhaustively for n<=8. All arithmetic is exact integer (delta_i and W are integers, +infinity modelled as None with an explicit comparator); no floats participate in any decision. The oracle is independent and triple-checked: exhaustive DFS enumeration of all 2^(n-2) v1->v_n paths, the solution's own subset closed form W - sum_{i in S} delta_i, and DAG relaxation in topological order all agree that the true shortest distance is 0 and that the 2^(n-2) path weights are distinct. Part 1 of the solution (the graph construction and its exponentially many distinctly-weighted paths) is therefore CONFIRMED correct; the refuted claim is strictly the Part-2 inference that exponentially many distinct path weights force exponentially many relaxations of d(v_n) on this family. The implementation's final distances agree with the oracle (d(v_n)=0) at every n, so this is a bound violation, not an output-correctness bug. Deterministic: no sampling, no seeds, identical output on every run.
